title: Local quasi-finiteness of a composite implies that of its first scheme map
statement: Let $X,Y,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms. If $g\circ f$ is locally quasi-finite in the scheme sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite], then $f$ is locally quasi-finite in that same sense, including its local finite-type condition. No hypothesis on $g$ and no quasi-compactness, separatedness or Noetherian hypothesis are imposed.

source.place: Tag 03WR, lemma-permanence-quasi-finite, final assertion (global local quasi-finiteness).

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$, and put $y=f(x)$ and $z=g(y)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open $W\subseteq Z$ containing $z$, then an affine open $V\subseteq g^{-1}(W)$ containing $y$, and then an affine open $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ containing $x$. These choices use only continuity and the affine-open basis, and do not assume intersections of affine opens are affine.

source.place: Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens); compatible affine neighborhoods in the reduction of Tag 03WR.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_Z(W)$, $B=\mathcal O_Y(V)$ and $C=\mathcal O_X(U)$. The restricted scheme maps induce $A\to B\to C$, whose composite is the ring map for $(g\circ f)|_U:U\to W$ by contravariant functoriality [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Apply (1) implies (2) of [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-affine-criterion] to $g\circ f$ and the affine pair $(U,W)$. Thus $A\to C$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $C$.

Let $\mathfrak r\subset C$ be any prime. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-four-rings] with $R=A$, $S=C$, $R^{\prime}=B$, $S^{\prime}=C$, and $S\to S^{\prime}$ the identity. The square commutes by the ring-map tower from step 2. Its generation hypothesis holds because every $c\in C$ is the product of the image of $c\in S$ and the image of $1\in R^{\prime}$. Both primes in $S$ and $S^{\prime}$ are $\mathfrak r$. The finite-type hypothesis and quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak r$ are supplied by step 2. The cited statement gives that $B\to C$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at $\mathfrak r$.

source.place: Tag 03WR, final sentence of proof; Algebra Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings), specialization R=A, S=S-prime=C, R-prime=B.

proof.text: Take in step 3 the prime of $C$ corresponding to $x\in U$. The affine neighborhoods $x\in U\subseteq X$ and $y\in V\subseteq Y$, with $f(U)\subseteq V$, now satisfy exactly the finite-type and quasi-finiteness conditions defining quasi-finiteness of $f$ at $x$ in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Since $x$ was arbitrary, that definition gives local quasi-finiteness of $f$. If $X$ is empty, its universal pointwise condition is vacuous.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03WR (lemma-permanence-quasi-finite), affine reduction using Tag 01TK and Algebra Tag 00PN; compatible neighborhoods spelled out using Schemes Tag 01IT.
